data.why: The repo bundles its own synthetic dataset at public/data/dataset.json, generated by scripts/generate_data.py and fetched client-side via src/data.ts; nothing needs to be supplied.

goals: Check whether a given promoter has already been tested in a particular cell type or tissue before planning new experiments
Compare a candidate promoter's expression against the reference promoter (CTRL-POS) across all tested contexts
Put up to six candidate promoters side by side across chosen contexts to shortlist the strongest performer
Toggle QC flags on and off to see whether a conclusion about a promoter's strength depends on questionable data
Identify promoter x context combinations that are untested (coverage gaps) versus tested-but-all-failed-QC
Export a chart panel as a high-resolution PNG for a slide or report

review.summary: The tree matches the README's three questions (has it been tested, how does it compare with the reference and other candidates, and does the conclusion survive QC) and adds plan-then-shortlist phases, export, clean general wording, and well-cut features. All 12 screens I sampled support their nodes, including the two tasks the second run left unconfirmed. Only minor citation and placement nits remain.
